text: NuA4, the major H4 lysine acetyltransferase (KAT) complex in *Saccharomyces cerevisiae*, is recruited to promoters to stimulate transcription initiation but also contains methylated-histone-binding domains. It is cotranscriptionally recruited to coding regions, dependent on physical association with elongating Pol II phosphorylated on its C-terminal domain by CDK7/Kin28, yet independent of Eaf1 and Tra1 (needed for promoter recruitment). Set1/Set2 histone methylation is dispensable for NuA4–Pol II interaction and targeting to some coding regions, but stimulates NuA4–histone interaction and H4 acetylation in vivo. The NuA4 KAT Esa1 mediates increased H4 acetylation, enhanced RSC occupancy, and histone eviction in coding sequences and stimulates transcription elongation rate; it cooperates with the SAGA H3 KAT Gcn5. This delineates an acetylation-mediated nucleosome remodeling/eviction pathway stimulating Pol II elongation in vivo.
